business_problem: Spendrups relied on schedule-based maintenance that could waste effort on healthy machines while missing more urgent issues, making it harder to improve production reliability, reduce waste, and support the brewer's sustainability goals.
solution_summary: Spendrups and IBM partner Epical rebuilt maintenance operations around IBM Maximo Manage, IBM Maximo Mobile, and IBM Maximo Scheduler so asset data and work planning could drive a shift from scheduled maintenance toward condition-based and predictive maintenance. The rollout covered three sites and paired software deployment with company-wide training and standardized working practices, because the transformation depended on both better tools and a new operating model. Production equipment generated detailed performance data; Maximo became the platform for capturing that information, turning it into schedules and prioritized tasks, and exposing it to technicians through mobile access to asset histories. Scheduler replaces spreadsheet coordination with rules-based planning, while dashboards built from Maximo data help management measure results. The architecture gives Spendrups a data-backed maintenance loop that supports reliability, efficiency, and lower environmental impact.

solution_components.name: IBM Maximo Manage
solution_components.role: Centralizes asset information, maintenance history, and actionable production data for planning and reliability improvement.

solution_components.name: IBM Maximo Mobile
solution_components.role: Delivers asset histories and operational context to field technicians while they work onsite.

solution_components.name: IBM Maximo Scheduler
solution_components.role: Automates scheduling and work-order management that had previously depended on manual planning.

data_flow: Performance data from production equipment is captured in Maximo Manage, used to prioritize maintenance tasks and schedules, coordinated through Maximo Scheduler, and delivered to technicians via Maximo Mobile so onsite work can be executed and recorded against current asset conditions.
business_outcome: Spendrups created a more reliable and efficient maintenance model, improved how lean teams use their time, and laid the groundwork for more sustainable brewing operations with stronger preventive and predictive insight.
architecture_clues: The rollout paired Maximo deployment with standardized maintenance practices across three sites.
Condition-based preventive maintenance became the target best practice before full predictive maintenance.
Epical built business-intelligence dashboards from Maximo data to measure results and process behavior.
